Experimental design / conditions: 3.0 g rape straw in 100 mL DI water with FeSO4·7H2O 0.2 M, urea 0.5 M, ascorbic acid 0.14 M; ultrasonicate; dry 80 °C; pyrolyze 600 °C, 10 °C/min, 120 min under N2. Typical tests: 0.2 g/L, 50 mg/L each target, 298 K, 150 rpm.
Reported result: Fe/N-BC SBET = 20.35 m2/g; pore volume = 0.048 cm3/g. Fe/N incorporation assessed by EDX, XRD, FTIR and XPS.
Source location (PDF page; table/figure): PDF p. 2 / printed p. 387; preparation §2.1 and characterization §3.1
Evidence status: Extracted from main PDF; SI not supplied
Caveat / follow-up: No yield or preparation cost; exact characterization details partly in Supplementary Text S1.

Experimental design / conditions: Single-solute isotherm; dose 0.2 g/L; CIP 0–200 mg/L; pH 6.0 ± 0.2; temperatures 298, 308, 318 K.
Reported result: Langmuir fitted qmax = 25.36 (298 K), 39.20 (308 K), 46.45 (318 K) mg/g; respective R2 = 0.92, 0.89, 0.90. Freundlich fits had R2 0.99, 0.98, 0.99.
Model / metric: Langmuir qmax vs Freundlich fit; not observed qe
Source location (PDF page; table/figure): PDF p. 5 / printed p. 390; Table 2, Fig. 2 caption
Evidence status: Extracted; qmax explicitly identified as model-derived
Caveat / follow-up: Do not compare directly with fixed-condition uptake or column capacity; peak qmax occurs at 318 K.

Experimental design / conditions: Single-solute isotherm; dose 0.2 g/L; Cu2+ 0–100 mg/L; pH 6.0 ± 0.2; 298, 308, 318 K.
Reported result: Langmuir fitted qmax = 27.92, 28.35 and 30.77 mg/g at 298, 308 and 318 K; respective R2 = 0.94, 0.97 and 0.94.
Caveat / follow-up: Cu2+ is not an antibiotic; include only as co-contaminant/competition evidence.

Experimental design / conditions: Binary isotherms; CIP 0–200 mg/L and Cu2+ 0–100 mg/L; dose 0.2 g/L; pH 6.0 ± 0.2; 298–318 K.
Reported result: At 318 K, fitted Langmuir qmax fell to 18.84 mg/g for CIP and 17.23 mg/g for Cu2+. Increasing CIP concentration from 0 to 200 mg/L lowered Cu2+ uptake from 20.51 to 4.66 mg/g when Cu2+ was fixed.
Value / units: 18.84 mg/g CIP; 17.23 mg/g Cu2+; Cu uptake 20.51 to 4.66 mg/g
Model / metric: Binary-system fitted qmax and observed competition trend
Source location (PDF page; table/figure): PDF pp. 5–6 / printed pp. 390–391; Table 2; §3.3.1–3.3.4; Fig. 3
Evidence status: Extracted; exact interpretation restricted to reported mixture
Caveat / follow-up: Competition is strong; binary and single-system values must remain separated.

Evidence domain: pH, ionic strength and water matrix
Experimental design / conditions: pH 2–6 and NaCl 0–100 mM; water-matrix test at 50 mg/L each in DI water, tap water and groundwater.
Reported result: Single system: CIP uptake highest around pH 5 at 20.20 mg/g; Cu2+ increased to 20.51 mg/g at pH 6. NaCl increased 0→100 mM: CIP 17.30→11.33 mg/g; Cu2+ 20.51→33.72 mg/g. Binary pH separation factors: SF(CIP) 7.42 at pH 2; SF(Cu2+) 0.14 at pH 2 and 3.82 at pH 6. Groundwater uptake 1.50× for CIP and 1.18× for Cu2+ vs DI; tap-water uptake slightly lower.
Value / units: As reported; units mg/g unless separation factor/fold-change
Model / metric: pH, ionic-strength, separation factor and matrix observations
Caveat / follow-up: Real-water tests are high-concentration spiked tap/groundwater, not real wastewater. Authors call CIP NaCl impact negligible although reported uptake changes by ~35%.

Experimental design / conditions: Kinetic tests at 298–318 K; 20 mg sorbent/100 mL, 50 mg/L target; at least triplicate; five sequential co-adsorption cycles.
Reported result: PSO frequently fitted better; XPS suggests changes in C–N, π–π*, C–O, M–O/C=O and Fe oxidation-state signals. Authors propose pore filling, π–π, electrostatics and H-bonding for CIP; iron-associated complexes/electrostatics for Cu2+. Cu2+ performance declines substantially after five cycles; CIP declines gradually.
Value / units: PSO R2 in single CIP tests 0.94–0.97; exact recycle values not captured from figure
Evidence status: Extracted with mechanism evidence rated indirect/proposed
Caveat / follow-up: PSO fit alone does not prove chemisorption; “reduction” of Cu requires verification from chemical-state evidence. No cost or regeneration-method detail.

Target / co-contaminant: CBZ, SMX, PAR (only SMX is antibiotic)
Experimental design / conditions: Dry primary paper-mill sludge + 50% ammonium lignosulfonate solution at 6:5 w/w; pyrolyze 500 °C 10 min under N2; KOH impregnate at 1:1 w/w; pyrolyze 800 °C 150 min under N2; acid/water wash; dry 105 °C 24 h; 0.5–1.0 mm granules.
Reported result: Virgin PSA-PA SBET = 671 m2/g, pore volume 0.37 cm3/g, DR micropore volume 0.27 cm3/g. Fixed bed 2.6 cm depth, ~3.56 g, 25 ± 1 °C; 5 mg/L feed; flow 4.3, 8.6 or 13.0 L/day in flow study.
Caveat / follow-up: Only SMX is an antibiotic; do not treat CBZ/PAR as antibiotic targets. Detailed preparation refers to prior article.

Evidence domain: Real wastewater / single and ternary feeds
Experimental design / conditions: Municipal biological WWTP effluent, filtered 0.45 μm; five campaigns March–June 2018; stored dark at 4 °C and used within 15 days; native target pharmaceuticals below detection, then spiked to 5 mg/L each. Wastewater pH ~7.3–7.7. Column flow 4.3 L/day; C/C0=0.1 threshold.
Reported result: Observed column qtotal in single wastewater solution: SMX 2.23 mg/g (t10%=0.10 d; breakthrough volume 0.45 L); CBZ 6.65 mg/g; PAR 4.46 mg/g. In ternary wastewater feed, SMX qtotal = 0.67 mg/g, CBZ 5.58 mg/g, PAR 8.57 mg/g.
Value / units: mg/g as integrated experimental column capacity; SMX values are antibiotic-relevant
Source location (PDF page; table/figure): PDF pp. 2, 5–7 / printed pp. 700, 703–705; §2.2–2.3; Table 1; Fig. 2
Caveat / follow-up: CBZ=antiepileptic, PAR=antidepressant. Breakthrough curves did not reach C/C0=1 within the test window; qtotal is not guaranteed true saturation capacity.

Experimental design / conditions: CBZ 5 mg/L; distilled water; flow rates 4.3, 8.6, 13.0 L/day; continuous fixed-bed.
Reported result: Observed qtotal = 39.91, 31.66, 19.95 mg/g and breakthrough time = 2.92, 0.83, 0.21 days, respectively. In wastewater at same flow rates, CBZ qtotal = 6.65, 7.00, 2.34 mg/g.
Model / metric: Observed integrated column values, not fitted qTH/qY
Caveat / follow-up: Distilled-water capacity is much higher than wastewater, consistent with matrix competition. CBZ is not antibiotic-specific evidence.

Experimental design / conditions: Exhausted PSA-PA after CBZ adsorption from distilled water; regenerate at 500 °C under N2 for 90 min; repeat fixed-bed adsorption at 4.3 L/day.
Reported result: CBZ qtotal: 39.91 mg/g virgin, 24.95 mg/g after first regeneration, 11.49 mg/g after second; SBET 671, 617 and 463 m2/g for cycles 0, 1 and 2; post-use cycle-2 area 391 m2/g.
Model / metric: Experimental column capacity and BET area
Caveat / follow-up: Authors recommend no more than one reuse cycle given thermal demand and capacity loss. No full energy/cost inventory.

Experimental design / conditions: Fitted Thomas, Yoon–Nelson and Yan models compared with experimental breakthrough curves.
Reported result: Example: CBZ in distilled water at 4.3 L/day, observed qtotal = 39.91 mg/g, Thomas qTH = 64.3 ± 1.2 mg/g and Yan qY = 59.6 ± 0.6 mg/g. Yan model generally fit best, but fitted capacities overestimate observed qtotal in several cases.
Value / units: mg/g; R2 per model in paper
Model / metric: Fitted model parameter vs experimentally integrated capacity
Caveat / follow-up: Curves often did not reach exhaustion; model predictions should not be substituted for measured integrated performance.

Adsorbent / material: KOH-activated dyeing-sludge biochar KSC-8; SC controls
Experimental design / conditions: Dewatered dyeing sludge (61.23% solids) dried 105 °C 72 h, ground 60 mesh; sludge:KOH 1:1 w/w; pyrolyze at 700/800/900 °C for 3 h, ramp 5 °C/min under N2; wash 3 M HCl for 6 h; rinse neutral, dry 75 °C overnight.
Reported result: SBET: unactivated SC-7/8/9 = 360.3/306.8/284.6 m2/g; activated KSC-7/8/9 = 791.2/1178.4/926.5 m2/g. KSC-8 pore volume = 0.74 cm3/g; pores described mostly <1 nm.
Caveat / follow-up: One sentence on PDF p. 7 prints 1078.4 m2/g while abstract, characterization and Table 2 show 1178.4 m2/g.

Experimental design / conditions: TC isotherm range 10–800 mg/L at 298 K; method describes 100 mL batch, shaker 180 rpm. Adsorbent mass/dose for batch tests is not clearly provided in main PDF.
Model / metric: Langmuir fitted qmax, not low-concentration observed uptake
Source location (PDF page; table/figure): PDF p. 6 / Table 1; §2.4 states isotherm concentrations and 298 K
Caveat / follow-up: Conclusion says 1081.3 mg/g at 278 K, while methods say isotherm tests at 298 K; SI needed. Do not rank without reporting dose and test concentration.

Experimental design / conditions: Temperature comparison with TC 100 mg/L; 298, 308 and 318 K. pH tests 3–11; KSC-8 pHpzc 4.4; TC pKa reported 3.3, 7.7, 9.7.
Reported result: Observed experimental uptake in temperature tests: 305.99 mg/g (298 K), 323.91 mg/g (308 K), 351.48 mg/g (318 K). Reported pH-5 uptake = 311.85 mg/g. PSO R2 = 0.997/0.999/0.996 vs PFO R2 = 0.910/0.937/0.913.
Model / metric: Observed qt,exp plus kinetic fits; condition details partly incomplete
Source location (PDF page; table/figure): PDF pp. 6–7 / Fig. 3, Fig. 4; Table S5 referenced but not supplied
Evidence status: Extracted from main text; dose/SI pending
Caveat / follow-up: PSO fit is not proof of chemisorption; the reported dose for these batch conditions is not clear in supplied main PDF.

Experimental design / conditions: Simulated matrix: glucose 200 mg/L COD, NH4Cl to 30 mg/L ammonia-N and NaCl 300 mg/L chloride. Actual tailwater reported COD 57.19 mg/L, ammonia-N 0.40 mg/L. Main text reports TC completely removed within 30 min. A separate cross-antibiotic test used 20 mg/L for CIP, SMZ and tilmicosin in Methods.
Reported result: Reported removal: 100% TC, CIP and SMZ; 96.34% tilmicosin (Fig. 4e). Actual tailwater TC reportedly completely removed within 30 min; source and exact test composition need clarification.
Caveat / follow-up: Do not assume all four removal percentages are from real wastewater. Actual tailwater source, starting antibiotic concentrations and details are not fully described in main PDF.

Experimental design / conditions: Regeneration using 100 mL solution with Fe2+ 2 mM and H2O2 100 mM at initial pH 3 for 3 h; five cycles.
Reported result: Body text: by cycle 5 regeneration efficiency = 86.88% and retained adsorption capacity = 86.35%; cycles 1–3 retained 100% removal. Abstract calls 86.35% the removal efficiency after five cycles.
Model / metric: Regeneration efficiency vs retained capacity vs removal efficiency
Caveat / follow-up: Do not collapse the three differently labelled percentages. Fenton reagents and spent liquid need to be included in process-cost/end-of-life analysis.

Experimental design / conditions: Fixed-bed: 0.25 g KSC-8 in 100 × 16 mm cylindrical vessel (80 mL volume); influent TC 10 mg/L, pH 5; flow 1.5 mL/min; nominal dose 3.13 g/L; HRT around 50 min.
Reported result: 13.59 L treated before TC reached 1 mg/L; reported capacity at this threshold = 543.46 mg/g. Separately stated maximum fixed-bed capacity = 1124.2 mg/g.
Model / metric: Breakthrough endpoint vs reported maximum column capacity
Caveat / follow-up: The 1124.2 mg/g value exceeds batch Langmuir qmax of 1081.3 mg/g and is described as nearly equal despite being higher; verify capacity integration, run duration and definitions.

Experimental design / conditions: Author estimate: reagents ~$3/kg adsorbent; pyrolysis energy ~25 kWh and associated cost ~$5.6/kg; total preparation cost ~$9/kg; compared with asserted average activated-carbon cost ~$28/kg.
Reported result: Reported combined cost ~$9/kg, vs paper-referenced average AC ~$28/kg.
Value / units: USD/kg per paper; kWh amount basis unclear
Caveat / follow-up: Functional unit, year/currency basis, energy-price assumptions, yield, acid washing, wastewater treatment, equipment, scale, regeneration and spent-media costs are not established in the main PDF.

Experimental design / conditions: Mechanism discussion based on pHpzc/zeta potential, pore structure, FTIR/XPS and pH behaviour.
Reported result: Authors propose pore filling, electrostatic interactions, hydrogen bonding and π–π interactions. Evidence is consistent with several interactions but does not quantify each contribution independently.
Model / metric: Proposed mechanism supported by characterization trends
Evidence status: Extracted; proposed mechanism not uniquely established
Caveat / follow-up: Paper's Eq. (2), PDF p. 3, prints removal R% = (C0−Ct)/Ct × 100; conventional formula uses C0 in denominator. Also temperature, BET area and regeneration labels conflict internally. Authors' removal/capacity calculations need confirmation.

Adsorbent / material: OTC-imprinted magnetic biochar (MBC@MIPs); MBC and non-imprinted MBC@NIPs controls
Experimental design / conditions: OTC template + methacrylic acid; EGDMA crosslinker; AIBN initiator. Deoxygenate, react at 60 °C for 24 h, magnetically separate, wash and vacuum-dry at 60 °C. Base MBC recipe refers to previous work/SI.
Reported result: SEM, FTIR, XRD, XPS, magnetic hysteresis and TGA support a polymer shell on magnetic biochar; authors report magnetic separation in under 10 s.
Evidence status: Extracted from main PDF; SI not supplied
Caveat / follow-up: Base-biochar recipe/yield and some characterization details are not fully present; no cost/energy inventory.

Experimental design / conditions: Dosage: 5 mg/L OTC, 25 °C, pH 6.50 ± 0.1; 0.1–1.0 g/L. pH test: 0.5 g/L, 5 mg/L OTC at 25 °C.
Reported result: Removal rose from 17.0% at 0.1 g/L to 89.37% at 0.5 g/L; 1.0 g/L gave marginal further gain. Removal at pH 6.34 ~89.4%, pH 3 41.6%, pH 10 26.8%.
Evidence status: Extracted from figure/caption and main text
Caveat / follow-up: Lab water only; not real wastewater. Removal is condition-specific, not capacity.

Experimental design / conditions: 0.5 g/L adsorbent, 2 mg/L OTC, 25 °C, pH 6.50 ± 0.1; 250 rpm; 6 h.
Reported result: For MBC@MIPs: PFO fitted qe 10.84 mg/g (R² 0.9805); PSO fitted qe 12.55 mg/g (R² 0.9995); narrative reports experimental uptake about 12.07 mg/g. About 70–90% uptake within 4 h.
Model / metric: Kinetic model-fitted capacities vs experimental uptake
Caveat / follow-up: PSO is a statistical fit, not proof of chemisorption; prose mixes mg/g and mg/L in places.

Experimental design / conditions: OTC isotherms span 1–200 mg/L. Abstract quotes 299 K; methods generally say 25 °C.
Reported result: MBC@MIPs Langmuir fitted qmax 67.89 mg/g (R² 0.9821); narrative gives experimental 60.19 mg/g at a cited condition. Table 2 lists MBC 38.34 mg/g but abstract/body report 38.84 mg/g; BC 8.96 mg/g; MBC@NIPs 41.09 mg/g.
Model / metric: Fitted qmax vs reported experimental uptake
Caveat / follow-up: Do not silently choose 38.34 vs 38.84 mg/g; check SI/curve for experimental uptake condition.

Target / co-contaminant: OTC, DOX, TC, CTC, NOR, MNZ; competing antibiotics
Experimental design / conditions: Individual test: 0.5 g/L, 4 mg/L antibiotic, 25 °C, 6 h; mixed antibiotic condition shown in Fig. 4.
Reported result: Individual uptake: OTC 11.97 mg/g; TC 4.01; DOX 7.28. Imprinting factors: OTC 5.64, DOX 2.93, TC 2.95, CTC 4.14, NOR 1.05, MNZ 1.34. In mixture, OTC uptake 6.10 mg/g and IF 6.70.
Caveat / follow-up: Controlled mixtures only, not real wastewater. Keep IF separate from capacity/removal.

Experimental design / conditions: Seven reuse cycles. Leaching protocol: 100 mg sorbent in 10 mL DI water for 24 h at pH 2–9; iron assessed by graphite-furnace AAS.
Reported result: Authors report 9.36% reduction in OTC binding over seven cycles. Leaching protocol is described but numerical iron results are not given in the accessible main-text details.
Model / metric: Reuse stability; leaching result not captured
Evidence status: Partial evidence; precise cycle values graphical; iron result unresolved
Caveat / follow-up: No real wastewater, column, cost estimate or numeric leaching result in main PDF.

Adsorbent / material: Bacterial-cellulose microfilament char / chitosan / polyethyleneimine crosslinked beads
Continuum stage: Stage 2/3 interface — biopolymer-based composite with hydrothermal char
Experimental design / conditions: Cellulose membrane hydrolysed with cold 64% H2SO4; 4 g filaments dispersed in 50 mL water, sonicated 1 h, pH 2, hydrothermal treatment 200 °C for 18 h (10 °C/min). Beads: 100 mL 1% chitosan in 2% acetic acid, PEI 1:1 molar ratio, 0.2 g char, 3 mL of 1% GA, drop into 1 M NaOH, wash/freeze-dry.
Reported result: A millimetre-scale crosslinked composite bead integrates char within the CS/PEI matrix.
Caveat / follow-up: No bead/char yield, energy inventory or preparation cost; some prior-method details/SI unavailable.

Adsorbent / material: BCM char/CS/PEI beads; PEI/CS bead and char controls
Experimental design / conditions: N2 adsorption, FTIR, EDX, SEM/TEM, TGA and zeta potential; beads 1.5–2 mm.
Reported result: BET area: PEI/CS 5.98 m²/g; BCM char 112.42 m²/g; composite beads 89.81 m²/g. Composite BJH pore volume 0.0991 cm³/g; C/O/N 44.95/27.05/28.00%; isoelectric point 9.3 for beads, 2.6 for char.
Caveat / follow-up: Reported pore-size around 68.4 Å is described as “sub-micropores”; terminology requires checking before repetition.

Experimental design / conditions: Typical time experiment: 4 mg in 15 mL (~0.267 g/L), 50 mg/L antibiotic, 298 K, pH 8 for TET and 6 for MET; pH tests from 3 to 9.
Reported result: At 10 mg/L and 90 min, abstract reports TET removal 99.13% and MET 90%; body reports TET 99.52% and MET 90%. TET pH optimum 8; MET pH optimum 6.
Caveat / follow-up: Do not choose 99.13% vs 99.52% silently. No real-water matrix experiment in main text.

Experimental design / conditions: Optimized condition in conclusion: 4 mg adsorbent in 15 mL (~0.267 g/L), 90 min, initial concentration 400 mg/L, 298 K; pH 8 TET/pH 6 MET.
Reported result: Empirical capacities 960.778 mg/g TET and 691.325 mg/g MET.
Model / metric: Empirical uptake at high starting concentration
Caveat / follow-up: Capacities are at 400 mg/L initial concentration, not environmental trace concentration.

Experimental design / conditions: Kinetic time series: 4 mg in 15 mL of 50 mg/L solution, optimal pH, 298 K. PFO, PSO, Avrami, Elovich, Bangham, IPD and LFD models compared.
Reported result: Table 2: PFO qcal 411.702 mg/g TET (R² .937) and 381.495 MET (.942); PSO qcal 204.081 TET (.998) and 188.67 MET (.992). Text reports practical kinetic uptake around 186 mg/g TET and 158 mg/g MET; staged Avrami fit R² up to .999.
Source location (PDF page; table/figure): PDF pp. 7–9; Table 2 and Fig. S7 cited
Caveat / follow-up: Do not mix these 50 mg/L kinetic values with 400 mg/L isotherm capacities. Multiple models fit; model fit alone does not prove mechanism.

Experimental design / conditions: Isotherms cover initial concentrations 10–400 mg/L; Langmuir, Freundlich, Temkin, Redlich–Peterson, Sips, Toth and others fitted.
Reported result: Table 3 Langmuir qmax,cal 990.099 mg/g TET (R² .996) and 666.66 MET (.997); Sips 918.26/.987 and 690.59/.985; Toth 880/.963 and 790/.991. Empirical values in conclusion are 960.778/691.325 mg/g.
Caveat / follow-up: Several isotherms fit well; keep model-derived and observed values distinct.

Experimental design / conditions: Mechanisms interpreted from pH/zeta potential and FTIR/EDX; regeneration uses repeated water/methanol washing. Article refers to 11 cycles but also gives metrics “over two cycles.”
Reported result: Authors propose electrostatic, π–π, hydrogen-bond and Lewis acid–base interactions. Conflicting regeneration: TET removal 96.7%→89.81% “over two cycles” and 92.86% total effectiveness, but elsewhere says removal reaches 63.22% after eleven cycles (65.37% of starting value).
Caveat / follow-up: Do not quote one settled 11-cycle retention value; the article notes solvent/post-treatment cost, bead stability and spent-media disposal.

Target / co-contaminant: AZ, CPX, SMX, TMP, TC; nutrients
Adsorbent / material: Sewage-sludge biochar at 550/700 °C; CAS or DMSO surface modification
Continuum stage: Stage 3 — solvent/chemical modified biochar; source-separated urine application
Experimental design / conditions: SS550/SS700 biochars supplied by UK Biochar Research Centre; modification screened across DMSO, ionic liquids and DES. Selected variants include SS550/SS700 CAS and SS550/SS700 DMSO. Exact pyrolysis and modifier recipes reference SI.
Reported result: SS700 pristine BET 32.21 m²/g; after modification 16.99 m²/g (CAS) and 20.27 m²/g (DMSO). Mean pore diameter 5.03 nm pristine, 5.67 nm CAS, 7.37 nm DMSO. Contact angles across samples 14.12–66.41°; modified chars more hydrophilic.
Caveat / follow-up: Modification reduces BET area while increasing mean pore diameter/hydrophilicity; full recipe/yield/cost absent from main text.

Adsorbent / material: CAS/DMSO-modified sewage-sludge biochar; later stage uses separate pristine char for nutrients
Continuum stage: Stage 3 — modified biochar; source-separated urine application
Experimental design / conditions: Fresh human urine diluted 1:1 with DI water to imitate flushed urine; antibiotics spiked. Isotherms: 20 mL, dose 0.1–20 g/L, each antibiotic 100 or 1000 µg/L, 30±1 °C, 180 rpm, 24 h. Kinetics: 5 g/L, 100–1000 µg/L. pH tests: 40 mg/40 mL, each antibiotic 25 µg/L, pH 3–11, 24 h.
Reported result: Triplicate experiments; kinetic figure uses pH 7. Stage 1 modified char targets antibiotics; separate pristine char used in stage 2 for nutrients.
Caveat / follow-up: Diluted, spiked human urine is a special source-separated matrix, not municipal wastewater effluent or untreated urine with native target concentrations.

Experimental design / conditions: Isotherm tests used µg/L-scale initial concentrations; Langmuir/Freundlich compared with Temkin and Redlich–Peterson.
Reported result: Reported cross-material maximum capacities: AZ 196.08 µg/g (SS700 CAS); TMP 370.37 µg/g (SS700 CAS); TC 833.33 µg/g (SS550 DMSO); SMX about 81 µg/g (SS700 DMSO); CPX about 263 µg/g (SS550 CAS).
Model / metric: Reported maximum/fitted capacities across selected variants
Source location (PDF page; table/figure): PDF pp. 1, 5–6; abstract and §3.3.1; Table S6 cited
Caveat / follow-up: Values at µg/L feed concentrations are not directly comparable to mg/L-scale capacity studies.

Target / co-contaminant: AZ, TMP, TC, SMX, CPX; ammonia/phosphate comparators
Experimental design / conditions: Table 1 gives SS700 CAS and SS700 results; global R² ranges for Langmuir/Freundlich are 0.42–0.99 and 0.51–0.99.
Reported result: SS700 CAS Langmuir Qm (µg/g): AZ 196.08, TMP 370.37, TC −151.52, SMX 80.00, CPX 120.48. Pristine SS700 Qm negative for all five antibiotics. SS700 CAS phosphate Qm also negative (−7.06 mg/g).
Caveat / follow-up: Negative fitted capacities are physically unusable; indicate poor model fit for those pairs and should not be listed as real capacities.

Experimental design / conditions: Kinetics at 5 g/L and pH 7 in Fig. 2; antibiotics 100–1000 µg/L. pH tests at 25 µg/L each, pH 3–11, 24 h, 30±1 °C.
Reported result: Authors report SS700 CAS antibiotic equilibrium at ~12 h; PSO R² range 0.68–0.99; Elovich R² 0.94–0.99. Adsorption strongest around pH 7. The separate nutrient stage reports ammonia uptake up to 60 mg N/g on SS550 biochar; phosphate adsorption low.
Value / units: µg/g antibiotic scale; mg N/g nutrient capacity
Model / metric: Kinetics, pH and separate nutrient uptake
Caveat / follow-up: Authors propose H-bonding, electrostatics and π–π interactions; these contributions are not separately quantified. Keep nutrient and antibiotic metrics separate.

Target / co-contaminant: AZ, CPX, SMX, TMP, TC; ammonia/phosphate
Experimental design / conditions: Loading: pH 7, 24 h, 1000 µg/L antibiotic, 5 g/L char, 30±1 °C. Regenerate with isopropanol at 5–20 g char/L IPA, 180 rpm for 24 h; five cycles.
Reported result: After cycle 5, CPX/TMP regeneration efficiencies <20%; AZ/SMX/TC roughly 40–50%. Authors advise not using regenerated char beyond three cycles. Phosphate was not extracted after cycle 2 in this procedure.
Caveat / follow-up: Abstract says <30% removal capacity after three cycles while body gives antibiotic-specific values after five cycles; preserve metric/time discrepancy. No solvent recovery/cost/LCA.

Experimental design / conditions: Stage 1 uses solvent-modified biochar for antibiotic capture; stage 2 uses separate pristine biochar for nutrient recovery from the remaining solution.
Reported result: Paper reports about 90% removal of antibiotics in stage 1. Some nutrient adsorption occurs in stage 1; stage 2 is designed for later nutrient capture. No full process-cost, solvent-recovery, energy inventory or LCA provided.
Caveat / follow-up: This is urine treatment rather than wastewater-effluent treatment. DMSO/DES/IL modification and isopropanol regeneration must be included in process sustainability analysis.
